'''Patrick Baeuerle''' (born 24 November 1957) is a German[[Molecular Biologist|molecular biologist]], [[immunologist]], professor and a biopharmaceutical entrepreneur. Baeuerle is known for his work on [[tyrosine sulfation]] of proteins,<ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last1=Baeuerle |first1=P A |last2=Huttner |first2=W B |title=Tyrosine sulfation is a trans-Golgi-specific protein modification. |journal=Journal of Cell Biology |date=1 December 1987 |volume=105 |issue=6 |pages=2655–2664 |doi=10.1083/jcb.105.6.2655 |pmc=2114704 |pmid=3121635 }}</ref> transcription factor [[NF-kappaB]],<ref name="P A Baeuerle 1994 141–179">{{cite journal |last1=Baeuerle |first1=P A |last2=Henkel |first2=T |title=Function and Activation of NF-kappaB in the Immune System |journal=Annual Review of Immunology |date=April 1994 |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=141–179 |doi=10.1146/annurev.iy.12.040194.001041 |pmid=8011280 }}</ref> and the development of bispecific T-cell engaging antibodies for therapy of cancer.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baeuerle |first1=Patrick A. |last2=Reinhardt |first2=Carsten |title=Bispecific T-Cell Engaging Antibodies for Cancer Therapy |journal=Cancer Research |date=15 June 2009 |volume=69 |issue=12 |pages=4941–4944 |doi=10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-09-0547 |pmid=19509221 |doi-access= }}</ref>

==Education==
Baeuerle earned his [[diploma]] in biology from the [[University of Konstanz]], Germany. He received his Ph.D. in [[biochemistry]] [[summa cum laude]], from [[LMU Munich]]. His postdoctoral training was with the Nobel Laureate [[David Baltimore]] at the Whitehead Institute at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], Cambridge, MA.<ref>{{Cite patent|pubdate=1989-03-01|inventor=Patrick A. Baeuerle, David Baltimore, Whitehead Institute For Biomedical Research|country=WO|number=1989008147|title=ACTIVITION OF NF-kB PRECURSOR}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baeuerle |first1=Patrick A. |last2=Baltimore |first2=David |title=Activation of DNA-binding activity in an apparently cytoplasmic precursor of the NF-κB transcription factor |journal=Cell |date=April 1988 |volume=53 |issue=2 |pages=211–217 |doi=10.1016/0092-8674(88)90382-0 |pmid=3129195 |s2cid=24771542 }}</ref>

==Career==
After his post-doctorate, Baeuerle led a research group at Gene Center in [[Martinsried]], Germany. In 1993, he became the professor of molecular biology, and was and the chairman at the medical faculty of the [[University of Freiburg]], Germany.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hall |first1=Stephen S. |title=Success Is Like a Drug |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/11/23/magazine/success-is-like-a-drug.html |work=The New York Times |date=23 November 1997 }}</ref>

Between 1996 and 2015, he served as head of [[drug discovery]] at Tularik Inc.,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/19005/title/Two-Distinct-Career-Paths-Offer-Clear-Choices/|title=Two Distinct Career Paths Offer Clear Choices|website=The Scientist|access-date=2017-10-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/26250/title/Reinventing-the-Antibody/flagPost/42617/|title=Reinventing the Antibody|website=The Scientist|access-date=2017-10-04}}</ref> as [[chief scientific officer]] at Micromet Inc.,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Perkel |first1=Jeffrey |title=New Lymphoma Drug Shows Promise |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/08/14/AR2008081401926.html |newspaper=Washington Post |date=14 August 2008 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.xconomy.com/boston/2016/12/08/tcr-therapeutics-unveils-new-cancer-therapy-approach-and-44-5m-round/#|title=TCR2 Therapeutics Unveils New Cancer Therapy Approach and $44.5M Round {{!}} Xconomy|date=2016-12-08|work=Xconomy|access-date=2017-10-04|language=English}}</ref> and as a vice president research for [[Amgen, Inc.|Amgen Inc.]]<ref name="endpts.com">{{Cite web|url=https://endpts.com/amgen-vet-patrick-baeuerle-inspires-a-45m-round-from-a-list-vcs-for-a-next-gen-io-drug-platform/|title=Amgen vet Patrick Baeuerle inspires a $45M round from A-list VCs for a next-gen I/O drug platform|website=endpts.com|language=English|access-date=2017-10-04}}</ref> in [[Munich, Germany]].

Baeuerle is the co-founder of the companies, iOmx AG, Harpoon Inc,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gormley |first1=Brian |title=Harpoon Therapeutics Snares $45 Million Series B for Prostate Cancer Treatment |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/harpoon-therapeutics-snares-45-million-series-b-for-prostate-cancer-treatment-1495753792 |work=WSJ |date=25 May 2017 }}</ref> '' ''TCR<sup>2</sup> Inc,<ref name=":0" /> Maverick Inc, and Cullinan LLC. He is one of the Managing directors at [[MPM Capital|MPM capital]], which is a Cambridge-based venture capital firm.<ref name="endpts.com"/><ref>{{cite news |title=MPM Names Drug Developer Patrick Baeuerle Managing Director |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/DJFVW00120150312eb3craxgo |work=Wall Street Journal |date=13 March 2015 }}</ref>

==Research Activities==

=== Tyrosine Sulfation ===
In 1987, Baeuerle showed that tyrosine sulfation is a frequent modification of secretory proteins that is added in the trans-Golgi compartment.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/19238914|title=Tyrosine sulfation of yolk proteins 1, 2, and 3 in Drosophila melanogaster (PDF Download Available)|website=ResearchGate|language=en|access-date=2017-10-04}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

=== Transcription factor NF-kappaB ===
Baeuerle deciphered the canonical pathway by which transcription factor NF-kappaB is activated and first described inhibitory subunit I-kappaB and the p65/RelA subunit.<ref name="P A Baeuerle 1994 141–179"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baeuerle |first1=Patrick A. |last2=Baltimore |first2=David |title=IκB: a Specific Inhibitor of the NF-κB Transcription Factor |journal=Science |date=28 October 1988 |volume=242 |issue=4878 |pages=540–546 |id={{ProQuest|213535026}} |doi=10.1126/science.3140380 |pmid=3140380 |bibcode=1988Sci...242..540B }}</ref> Baeuerle is said to be one of the inventors of the controversial NF-kappaB.<ref>{{cite patent|title=Nuclear factors associated with transcriptional regulation|pubdate=Jun 25, 2002|inventor-last=Baltimore|inventor2-last=Sen|inventor3-last=Sharp|inventor-first=David|inventor2-first=Ranjan|inventor3-first=Phillip A.|country=US|number=6410516}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://worldwide.espacenet.com/publicationDetails/biblio?CC=US&NR=6410516&KC=&FT=E&locale=en_EP|title=Espacenet - Bibliographic data|website=worldwide.espacenet.com|language=en|access-date=2017-10-04}}</ref> He along with his team showed that NF-kappaB is an [[oxidative stress]]-responsive transcription factor and described a functional role of NF-kappaB in the nervous system.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.de/citations?user=Z2atVAEAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Patrick A. Baeuerle - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.de|access-date=2017-10-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schreck |first1=Ralf |last2=Albermann |first2=Kaj |last3=Baeuerle |first3=Patrick A. |title=Nuclear Factor Kb: An Oxidative Stress-Responsive Transcription Factor of Eukaryotic Cells (A Review) |journal=Free Radical Research Communications |date=January 1992 |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=221–237 |doi=10.3109/10715769209079515 |pmid=1473734 }}</ref>

=== Cancer Therapy ===
Baeuerle lead the development of BiTE antibody Blincyto® (blinatumomab; AMG 103)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baeuerle |first1=Patrick A. |last2=Kufer |first2=Peter |last3=Bargou |first3=Ralf |title=BiTE: Teaching antibodies to engage T-cells for cancer therapy |journal=Current Opinion in Molecular Therapeutics |date=February 2009 |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=22–30 |pmid=19169956 }}</ref> which is approved by the US FDA for treatment of relapsed/refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Swaminathan |first1=Nikhil |title=Antibody Drug Unleashes Tumor-Killer T Cells |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/antibody-drug-unleashes-tumor-killer-t-cells/ |work=Scientific American |date=15 August 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Highfield |first1=Roger |title=Patients 'free from cancer' after immune-boost treatment |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/science/science-news/3349596/Patients-free-from-cancer-after-immune-boost-treatment.html |work=The Telegraph |date=14 August 2008 }}</ref> He has invented various antibody-based constructs that are designed to engage cytotoxic T cells for lysis of cancer cells.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baeuerle |first1=Patrick A. |last2=Reinhardt |first2=Carsten |title=Bispecific T-Cell Engaging Antibodies for Cancer Therapy |journal=Cancer Research |date=15 June 2009 |volume=69 |issue=12 |pages=4941–4944 |doi=10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-09-0547 |pmid=19509221 |doi-access= }}</ref>
